headline: Tariff refunds flatter a profit rebound as segments diverge
summary_short: NOV's Q2 2026 revenue was $2,134M, up 4.0% sequentially but down 2.5% year-over-year, while operating profit jumped 35% y/y to $193M — a gain that included roughly $40M of one-time tariff refunds — lifting net income to $112M ($0.31 diluted EPS).
summary_long: Energy Equipment revenue grew 1% y/y on strong offshore-project execution and a richer mix; Energy Products and Services fell 5% y/y as Middle East disruption cut capital-equipment sales, partly offset by drill-bit and artificial-lift share gains. Operating profit ($193M, +35% y/y) and company-defined Adjusted EBITDA ($283M, +$31M y/y) both benefited from a combined ~$40M tariff-refund credit in cost of revenue. Net income rose only $4M y/y to $112M as the effective tax rate jumped to 26.1% from 0.9%. H1 operating cash flow was -$9M on working-capital swings; capex was $146M, buybacks $130M, dividends $97M. Backlog fell $220M y/y to $4.08B. No numeric forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Sequential revenue growth and a year-over-year profit rebound were driven mainly by a combined ~$40M tariff-refund credit and stronger offshore-project execution in Energy Equipment.

Y/y decline was driven by Energy Products and Services (-5%) on Middle East-linked disruption to capital-equipment sales; Energy Equipment (+1%) offset part of it on offshore-project execution and a favorable mix.
Gain reflects strong offshore-project execution and a favorable sales mix in Energy Equipment, plus a combined ~$40M tariff-refund benefit recorded in cost of revenue across both segments.
Net income grew only modestly against the large operating-profit gain because the effective tax rate rose to 26.1% from 0.9% a year ago, when a tax-reserve release had lowered the prior-year rate.
Operating cash flow swung to -$9M in H1 2026 from +$326M in H1 2025, primarily on working-capital changes in receivables, inventories, payables, and accrued liabilities.
